title: Lifting a prescribed pair of finite free chain maps
statement:
Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], P a cochain complex of O_Y-modules
[def-pc-derived-category] with finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module], supported
in [0,d], and Q the single complex O_Y^r in degree i. For y in Y let T denote termwise
pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] along Y.fromSpecStalk y. Given arbitrary chain maps
f:TP→TQ and g:TQ→TP, there are an open V containing y, chain maps fV:P|V→Q|V and
gV:Q|V→P|V, and complex isomorphisms eP:S(P|V)≅TP, eQ:S(Q|V)≅TQ, where S is pullback
along V.fromSpecStalkOfMem y hyV, such that S(fV)=eP.hom;f;eQ.inv and
S(gV)=eQ.hom;g;eP.inv. No inverse or homotopy condition is assumed.

source.place: Proof, first two paragraphs: local unit-entry cancellation and extension of the finite calculation; finite matrix coefficient extension and chain equations

proof.text: On an affine neighbourhood of y choose the finite bases supplied by the free-term hypotheses. Under the affine quasicoherent correspondence the components of the given maps f and g are matrices over O_{Y,y}. P is supported in [0,d] and Q in {i}, so only finitely many entries and commutativity equations are needed. Uses [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

For each matrix entry use the stalk representation criterion to choose a section near y, and intersect these finitely many neighbourhoods. For each chain commutativity equation take the difference of its two matrix expressions. Every entry has zero germ because f and g are chain maps. The germ equality criterion supplies a smaller neighbourhood for each entry. Intersect the finite family of these neighbourhoods. Uses [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

The represented matrices define fV and gV on this intersection. Outside the support there is a zero source or target, so the components and commutativity equations are uniquely determined. Pullback-composition, V.fromSpecStalkOfMem_ι and restriction-pullback comparison give the isomorphisms eP and eQ. Entrywise representation of the given f and g gives the two exact conjugacy equations. Uses [def-weil-pbc-free-module], [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction].

lean.statement:
theorem exists_restrict_chainMap_pair_of_stalk
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (P : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hge : P.IsStrictlyGE 0) (hle : P.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ s : ℕ, Nonempty
      (P.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s))))
    (i : ℤ) (r : ℕ) (y : Y)
    (f : (((Modules.pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj P) ⟶
      (((Modules.pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj
      (SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))))
    (g : (((Modules.pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj
      (SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))) ⟶
      (((Modules.pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj P)) :
    ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (hyV : y ∈ V),
      let R := (restrictFunctor V.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      let S := (Modules.pullback (V.fromSpecStalkOfMem y hyV)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      let T := (Modules.pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      let Q := ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor Y.Modules i).obj
      (SheafOfModules.free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
      ∃ (eP : S.obj (R.obj P) ≅ T.obj P) (eQ : S.obj (R.obj Q) ≅ T.obj Q)
        (fV : R.obj P ⟶ R.obj Q) (gV : R.obj Q ⟶ R.obj P),
        S.map fV = eP.hom ≫ f ≫ eQ.inv ∧ S.map gV = eQ.hom ≫ g ≫ eP.inv
